prompt: The new search is in the deployed code but hidden behind an on/off switch.
why: The code is deployed, but a switch decides whether users see it. Shipping code separately from turning it on is a feature flag.
trap: It's already deployed, so it isn't a branch.

prompt: The feature is turned on for 5% of users first.
why: Turning a feature on for a small share of users first limits the damage if something's wrong. Gradual rollouts are done with feature flags.

prompt: When the new page caused errors, they switched it off without redeploying.
why: They turned the page off with a switch instead of shipping new code. Being able to switch a feature off instantly is what feature flags are for.
trap: A revert needs a new deploy.

prompt: Unfinished code merges to main but stays dark until it's ready.
why: Unfinished code can merge to main because a flag keeps it hidden. That lets teams merge often without exposing half-built features.
trap: It's merged, so not hidden on a branch.

prompt: Beta testers see the new editor; everyone else sees the old one.
tells: Beta testers see the new editor
why: Different users see different versions depending on who they are. Turning a feature on for one group is a feature flag.

prompt: A config setting decides whether the new checkout flow is shown.
why: A setting, not the code itself, decides whether the new flow is shown. A setting that switches a feature on or off is a feature flag.
